neighbours.label: The predicate word (verb or auxiliary) of a qualified or contrastive claim ('but not determined', 'can only be improved', 'what X gets right'), vs the same content stated flatly
fire: Prices are influenced, but not controlled, by the central bank.
What the old model gets wrong is its view of risk.
The river can only be crossed if the water level drops.
Talent is shaped, but not fixed, by early training.
What this approach gets right is its focus on the patient.
The project can only succeed if every team cooperates.
Our habits are guided, but not dictated, by our genes.
Peace can only be secured if both sides disarm.
quiet: Prices are controlled by the central bank.
The old model has a simple view of risk.
The river was crossed by the soldiers at dawn.
Talent comes from years of early training.
This approach focuses on the patient.
The project started last week with every team.
Our habits are linked to our genes.
The treaty was signed by both sides in May.

predictions: Contrastive or restricted predicates 0.4-1.0; flat restatements under 0.2.
notes: Card: peaks on ' not' in 'influenced, but not determined', ' gets' in 'What Marxism gets right', ' be' in 'can only be improved if'. Probe: 'gets right' 0.997, 'but not determined' 0.890, 'can only be improved if' 0.849, 'is compromised' 0.437; flat versions 0.014-0.336.
